hook: SCP-2935 is an exploration story told almost entirely through mission transcripts, and it rewards a slow, patient read. The setup is simple: a cave in rural Indiana opens onto a version of our world that is quietly wrong. Try to read it in one sitting, and listen to what is missing as closely as to what the team finds.
whyItMatters: It sits among the most highly rated articles on the English wiki and is a standout of the dead-world subgenre. Much of its weight comes from the canon itself: the team walks through familiar Foundation sites and checks on anomalies readers already know, and finds them all equally still. It shows how much dread a writer can build with no monster ever appearing on the page.
thingsToNotice: The moment the team reaches SCP-682 works as a measuring stick, since the wiki's most unkillable creature is the clearest proof of how total the event was. Agent Keller quietly collects oddities across the logs, from a jammed cell door to a body that does not match the others and a warning posted after everyone should have been gone. The hidden audio file at the end flips the whole expedition into a warning about our own side, and its last line is aimed straight at whoever is listening. Notice how often the logs mention the lack of birdsong and insects.

related.note: Its fate here is the clearest sign of how absolute the event was.
Another lone voice stranded in a reality with nobody left in it.
Another trip into a Foundation site from a reality that went wrong.
